script.title: Wars Saved the Leaning Tower of Pisa From Toppling
sentences: Wars may be why the Leaning Tower of Pisa still stands.
Its foundations were laid on 9 August 1173.
By 1178, when building reached the second floor, the tower had already begun to sink.
Its foundation was only three metres deep, in weak, unstable soil.
The tilt kept growing, reaching 5.5 degrees by 1990.
Then the work stopped for the better part of a century, because Pisa kept fighting Genoa, Lucca and Florence.
That pause gave the soil time to settle; otherwise, the tower would almost certainly have toppled.
So the tower owes its life to a war.
script.description:
The Leaning Tower of Pisa began sinking by its second floor.
A century-long pause, forced by wars, likely saved it.
claims_en: The foundations of the tower were laid on 9 August 1173.
In 1178 the tower began to sink after construction progressed to the second floor.
The foundation was a mere three metres, set in weak, unstable subsoil.
By 1990 the tilt had reached 5.5 degrees.
Construction was halted for the better part of a century as Pisa was almost continually engaged in battles with Genoa, Lucca and Florence.
This allowed time for the soil to settle; otherwise the tower would almost certainly have toppled.
